evals.prompt: Our CEO came back from a Tokyo trip convinced we need Japanese docs. Numbers from analytics for Ironvale (API gateway, about 800 docs pages on Hugo): 38% of docs sessions come from Japan. Browser language ja is 12% of sessions. Quickstart completion is 41% for Japan sessions versus 44% for English-browser readers. Nobody on the team reads Japanese. The plan on the table is to run all 800 pages through an LLM once, publish under /ja/, and fix things as people complain. CEO wants a yes or no by Friday. Can you write up the decision?
evals.expected_output: A per-locale decision that reads the 38% country share as location, not need: the 12/38 browser-language ratio and the 3-point quickstart gap both fall under the skill's baselines, so ja is classified no barrier shown and declined with a written reopen condition, the one-shot 800-page dump is rejected as off the ladder, and source hardening is the action that serves Japanese readers now.
expectations: Does not recommend translating the docs on the strength of the 38% Japan session share, and states that country share says where readers are, not that they need a translation
Divides the 12% ja browser share by the 38% Japan session share (about a third) and reads it as under the one-half baseline, meaning most of those readers run another browser language
Reads the 3-point quickstart completion gap (41% vs 44%) as under the 5-point baseline, so no comprehension barrier is shown
Labels the one-half ratio threshold and the 5-point and 10-point gap thresholds as baseline figures, distinct from the user's measured figures
Classifies ja as 'no barrier shown' and sets the decision to declined rather than launch or gated
States a reopen condition next to the refusal, such as the engagement gap opening past about 10 points, support tickets or forum posts arriving in Japanese, or a named deal in Japan
Asks for the language-of-demand signal (support tickets, forum posts, community chat or search queries written in Japanese) before closing the decision
Asks whether non-language causes of the gap were ruled out first: signup or payment friction, region availability, latency, phone verification, export rules
Rejects the one-shot machine translation of all 800 pages as not on the ladder, because it carries continuous MT's accuracy risk with none of its freshness
Recommends source hardening as the action to take now: plain global English, one term per concept, a glossary, no idioms, and translate="no" on code
Notes that search-engine snippet machine translation has excluded Japanese, so it does not count as a substitute for this market
Does not propose a conditional or partial launch, since no Japanese-fluent reviewer exists
States that the default answer is not yet until the browser-language, engagement and demand signals show need

Asks whether the product itself (UI, CLI output, error messages, support, billing) is localized, because a translated quickstart that ends in an English console leaves the reader switching languages mid-task

evals.prompt: Lanternfish is an open-source message broker I maintain alone. Docs are Docusaurus, about 220 pages. This week two contributors from São Paulo opened PRs translating the intro and the install guide into Portuguese and said they'd happily do the rest over the next couple of months. I don't read Portuguese. I'd like to say yes. What do I need to set up so I can merge these and keep going?
evals.expected_output: A community-program plan for pt-BR gated on ownership: two named Portuguese-fluent reviewers, review rights scoped to the locale directory, a progress page, an escalation path, licence terms translators accept, a source-commit pin on every page enforced in CI from the first merge, and a page order that starts with the critical path rather than the whole tree.
expectations: Promotes the community program rung because the project is open source and volunteers are already translating unprompted
Requires two named Portuguese-fluent reviewers before the locale launches, so no translator approves their own change
Does not count the maintainer as a pt-BR reviewer, since they do not read Portuguese
Scopes the volunteers' review and approval permissions to the pt-BR locale directory only
Requires a progress page showing which pages are translated and which are current
Requires a written escalation path for when the volunteer maintainers go silent
States that translations inherit the docs licence and names the contribution agreement or licence terms translators accept
Names the locale as pt-BR rather than generic Portuguese or pt-PT
Requires a source-commit pin in the front matter of every translated page from the first merged PR, with the drift check failing CI on no-pin and unknown-pin from day one
Gives the Docusaurus layout for the drift check, with the locale directory under i18n/pt-BR/docusaurus-plugin-content-docs/current (or the equivalent path) rather than a sibling docs/pt-br tree
States that the community program ranks last on durability because the cohort is the locale: when its maintainers leave, coverage freezes and rots
Writes the freeze-then-retire rule for when the last named reviewer leaves and no replacement is found within one quarter
Requires published owner names and a contact for translation problems before launch
Marks the locale gated until every gate item closes, listing each missing item with its closing action and expected date, rather than treating the merged PRs as a launch
Orders the page set to start with quickstart, install, auth, top task pages and site UI strings, and keeps contributor docs and the docs-site changelog untranslated

evals.prompt: We have a ja locale for Harrowgate (our CI product) docs, about 140 translated pages in docs/ja mirroring docs/en, Hugo. Freshness has been a mess. My plan: add a translated_at date to each ja page, and a CI job that flags any page where the en file's git modification date is newer than translated_at. Also our en how-to pages have last_verified: 2026-09-12 in front matter, and I'd like to copy that into the ja versions so Japanese readers see the page was verified. We tag releases, so I'll record source_version: v3.2 on each page. CI runs on a shallow checkout (fetch-depth 1) for speed. Does this plan hold?
evals.expected_output: A rejection of every date-based element: drift is detected from source history after a per-page commit-hash pin, never from file dates; a tag is not a valid pin; last_verified is never copied into a translation and source stamps render only while the pin is current; CI needs full history; and the existing backlog is handled with --since so only new or edited pages can fail the build.
expectations: Rejects comparing file dates, stating that any edit to a translation (even adding a stale marker) makes it look newer than its source, so date comparison reports drift as freshness
Replaces the date comparison with a per-page pin to the source commit hash and a check of source history after that pin
Rejects v3.2 as a pin because a tag or branch name resolves to a moving ref, which the drift check reports as unknown-pin
States the pin is the source file's last commit at the moment translation starts, never HEAD when the translator finishes
States the pin may be bumped only once every source change up to that commit has been applied to the translation, because bumping it without the content change hides drift
Rejects copying last_verified into the ja pages because the translation would claim a test run nobody did in Japanese
Says to render the source page's tested-version stamps with wording that attributes them to the source page, only while the drift check reports the page current
Says the outdated banner replaces the stamps once the source page moves
Allows locale-specific stamps (such as locale_tested_with or locale_last_verified) only when someone re-ran the procedure in a localized environment
States the drift check refuses a shallow clone and that CI needs full history (fetch-depth: 0)
Recommends running the check with --since <ref> so only ja pages added or edited after that ref can fail the build while the 140-page backlog gets pinned, then dropping --since once it is
Gives the drift-check invocation with --source docs/en and --locale ja=docs/ja
Names the statuses the check reports, including at least behind, far, no-pin and unknown-pin
Recommends setting --far from the docs set's commits per release rather than keeping the default of 5
Gives banner wording that says the English page has changed since the translation and puts the link to the English page in the first line, shown in Japanese

evals.prompt: Bridgewater Signals sells a telemetry platform. We just signed a contract with a German federal agency that requires German-language documentation for the Ingest and Access Control modules (that wording is in the contract) before go-live in 5 months. Our docs: 1,100 pages, three versions live (v4, v5, v6), about 30 docs commits a week on v6, two-week release cycle. One German-speaking solutions engineer, Lotte, can give maybe 6 hours per release. We were going to run everything through an LLM and let Lotte skim. What should the plan look like?
evals.expected_output: A plan that promotes full human translation for exactly the contract-named scope, keeps everything else to at most a critical-path pack given 30 commits a week and a 6-hour ceiling, translates v6 only with v4 and v5 falling back to English, sizes the set with the steady-state and launch-load formulas, routes Access Control pages to pre-publication human review, and gates the locale on a second independent reviewer.
expectations: Promotes full human translation for the contract-named scope (Ingest and Access Control modules) above every other rung, because a contract naming the language promotes it
Keeps the rest of the 1,100 pages off full human sync, with at most a critical-path pack, because high source churn plus a low effort ceiling deletes full-set rungs
Translates only the latest version (v6); v4 and v5 fall back to the source language
Runs the steady-state check as a formula: pages in the set changed per release times re-review hours per changed page must not exceed Lotte's 6 hours per release

Runs the launch-load check as a formula: (pages plus UI-string page-equivalents) times first-review hours divided by 6 hours per release equals releases until launch, compared with the 5-month deadline
Labels the 15-30 minutes per changed page, one hour per page on first review and one page-equivalent per 300 UI strings as baselines to replace with Lotte's own pace after the first release
Flags that a single reviewer fails the two-reviewer gate item and names the closing action: a vendor with an independent quality reviewer, or a second fluent hire or contractor
States that a vendor pipeline whose quality reviewer is independent of the translator meets the two-reviewer item, labelled as a baseline
Routes Access Control (security and authentication) pages to human review before publication, not to a page-view threshold
Masks code blocks before any LLM translation and verifies per page that code-fence count, link count and heading count match the source
Cites the published evaluation of LLM-translated READMEs (structural, code or URL damage in 16-50% of files while semantic scores stayed high) as a sourced figure
Marks the de locale gated with the missing items, closing actions and expected dates, rather than launching conditionally
Refuses 'Lotte skims' as the review model for the contract scope
Scales --far to the commits per release (about 60 on a two-week cycle at 30 commits a week) rather than keeping the default of 5
Ships the pin field names and the drift-check CI step in the plan before any page is translated

evals.prompt: We launched Spanish docs for Quillstone (our payments SDK) last month and reviews are mixed. Setup: Nuxt site, when Accept-Language says es we redirect to /es/. We translated everything including the 400-page API reference, CLI flags (our translator rendered --dry-run as --simulacion, which reads nicely), and error messages so they're natural Spanish. Headings are in Spanish so anchors are too. We indexed /es/ the day it went live. Users complain they can't find stuff. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: A diagnosis naming each broken rule: the auto-redirect replaced by a suggestion plus remembered switcher, CLI flags restored to source form, error strings quoted verbatim with Spanish alongside, anchors restored to English with explicit IDs, the API reference cut back to top-traffic pages or none, search exposure tied to the first review pass, and the variant, label, glossary and ownership gaps asked about.
expectations: Replaces the Accept-Language auto-redirect with a dismissible language suggestion plus a persistent switcher that remembers the reader's choice
States that auto-redirect traps readers and that crawlers send no language preference
Restores CLI flags to their source form (--dry-run), stating that identifiers, CLI flags, HTTP headers, config keys and product names are never translated
Requires error messages quoted verbatim as the product prints them, with the Spanish translation alongside, so the reader can search the string they see
Restores heading anchors to the source language with explicit IDs so links from support replies and other locales survive
Recommends cutting the API reference translation back to top-traffic pages only or none, citing the precedent of guides translated into 16 languages with reference left untranslated
Asks which variant the audience needs (es-ES or es-419) or states the variant decision explicitly
Requires a translation label on every page naming how it was translated, stating the English page is authoritative, with a one-click link to it and a way to report a translation problem
States that a new locale is exposed to search only after its first review pass, not on launch day
Adds a glossary recording every do-not-translate term with the decision and who made it
Asks whether every page carries a source-commit pin and whether a drift check runs
Defers screenshots and diagrams rather than translating them
Routes hreflang and canonical mechanics to samber/developer-relations-skills@docs-seo rather than fixing them inline
Routes security, authentication and billing pages (a payments SDK) to human review before publication
Asks for two named Spanish-fluent reviewers and a named person allowed to pull the locale before treating it as launched

evals.prompt: Status check on Fernhollow's localized docs. ja: owned by Aiko and Ren on our Tokyo support team, about 60 pages. ko: was run by a community volunteer, Minjun, who stopped responding in June; 45 pages, last touched April. Leadership asked for a dashboard with 'locale success metrics'. I'd rather keep ko visible, it still gets traffic and pulling it feels like we're giving up. What should I report and what do I do with ko?
evals.expected_output: A KPI set measured against a same-market source-language control (adoption, outcome, freshness by pin, quality per 1,000 views) with a two-quarter kill rule, and a ko decision that applies the last-reviewer rule: freeze read-only with a banner and retire with redirects unless a replacement is named, with revival only through the full launch gate.
expectations: Measures each locale against a control: the same pages read in the source language by the same market
Reports adoption as the share of candidate-language sessions staying on locale pages versus switching to the source page
Reports outcome as quickstart completion or time to first API call for locale readers, before versus after launch
Reports freshness as the percentage of pages current by pin, with the 80% of the critical-path pack target labelled as a baseline
Reports quality as translation-problem reports per 1,000 views
Writes the kill rule: adoption or freshness below target for two consecutive quarters retires the locale, with redirects to the source pages
Applies the last-reviewer rule to ko: freeze read-only with a banner, then retire if no replacement is named within one quarter of the reviewer leaving
Does not keep ko live as-is, because it has no owner and nobody allowed to approve changes
Specifies ko retirement as redirecting every ko URL to the source page and removing ko from the language switcher
States that retirement is one-way: a retired locale is revived only through the full launch gate, never by unfreezing old pages
Cites the MDN cut of 21 unmaintained locales with an estimated traffic loss under 2% as a sourced precedent
Asks whether ko and ja pages carry source-commit pins and computes freshness from the drift check, not from last-touched dates
Checks that ja still has a written retirement threshold and a named person allowed to pull the locale
Does not treat ko's traffic as evidence the locale works without the source-language control comparison

evals.prompt: Okay so I've done the homework. Marrowick (our feature-flag SaaS, 300 docs pages, Mintlify) has French: 22% of sessions from France, Belgium and Switzerland, fr browser share 17%, quickstart completion 48% for fr-browser readers vs 61% for English, around 40 French support tickets a month. Product UI is in French already. Claire and Yannis on our Paris team can each give 5 hours per two-week release. Something live within 6 months, and this is a standing thing, not a one-off. Just give me the answer: do we use a human translation agency or an LLM pipeline?
evals.expected_output: A refusal to answer the binary before brainstorming: fr is classified barrier confirmed with owners named, the ruled-out rungs are named, two or three bundles are presented with rung, page set, owner and standing hours, one is recommended with what eliminated the others, and the user is asked to pick before any page is chosen.
expectations: Announces brainstorming mode and withholds the final recommendation until candidate bundles are presented
Names the rungs deleted by the answers and why: the community program (no volunteer cohort, not open source) and full human sync (no contract or regulation names French)
Presents two or three candidate bundles for fr, each stating its rung, the page set it covers, the owner and the standing hours it costs
Recommends one bundle and names what eliminated each alternative
Asks the user to choose a bundle before selecting pages

Reads the 17/22 browser-to-country ratio (about three quarters) as above the one-half baseline and the 13-point quickstart gap as above the 10-point baseline, classifying fr as barrier confirmed, owner named
Recommends source hardening for every market alongside the critical-path pack as the default
States the move-up condition: the pack's KPIs hold for two release cycles and the owners have spare review hours
Reframes the agency-versus-LLM question as a choice of rung, page set and review model rather than a binary
States the efficiency order of the ladder with source hardening first and full human sync last
States the value, effort or durability orderings separately from the efficiency order rather than one blended rank
Reads the user's answers back in one line and asks no question they already answered
Runs the steady-state capacity check against the 10 reviewer hours per release that Claire and Yannis supply
Labels the 13-point gap and the 40 tickets a month as measured, and the thresholds they are compared against as baseline

evals.prompt: Thornbury is a Python data-validation library. Docs are Sphinx; translations live in locale/ja/LC_MESSAGES/*.po via sphinx-intl, and the Japanese team keeps their PO files in a separate repo, thornbury-docs-ja. A lot of our pages pull in shared .rst snippets with .. include::. I want to add the translation-drift-check.py script from your plan to CI so we can see which Japanese pages are behind. How do I wire it?
evals.expected_output: A redirection: the per-file pin and the script apply to mirrored file trees, not gettext PO workflows, so freshness comes from fuzzy and untranslated counts; the separate repository falls outside the script regardless; included snippets count as changes to every page rendering them; and the freshness target, banner, fallback and retirement rules still apply in PO terms.
expectations: States that gettext PO workflows are out of the script's scope and uses the PO files' fuzzy and untranslated counts as the freshness measure instead
Explains that the per-file source-commit pin and the drift script apply to mirrored file trees, which this layout is not
Notes that translations kept in a separate repository fall outside the script regardless, because source and translations must share one git repository with full history
Says to pin the same way (a source commit hash) and diff against the source repository's history when translations live in a separate repo
Flags that a changed .. include:: snippet changes every page that renders it, so those shared sources must be pinned and checked too
Notes that the script does not track includes, partials or generated content even where it does apply
Does not give a --locale ja=locale/ja/LC_MESSAGES invocation as the wiring
Still requires a written freshness target and a retirement threshold expressed in PO terms (such as a share of fuzzy or untranslated strings)
Notes that untranslated gettext strings fall back to English, so a partial translation can publish, and that the outdated label and fallback rules still apply
Cites the Python documentation precedent: gettext fuzzy marking with English fallback, and a required content set translated before the language switcher appears
Keeps the rule that file modification dates are never compared
Maps the script's current, behind and far statuses to the PO workflow's clean, fuzzy and untranslated counts rather than dropping the status model

evals.prompt: Saltmarsh is a cloud backup CLI plus web console. Big push into the Gulf: a reseller in Riyadh says Arabic docs would close three deals. Console and CLI output are English only, no plans to change that. We have an Arabic-speaking SE, Omar, who can review. Docs are 180 pages on Docusaurus. Scope me an Arabic docs locale.
evals.expected_output: A scope that starts from the English-only product gap and the single reviewer: the locale is gated on a second named reviewer, the page set is sized from Omar's hours rather than 180 pages, UI strings and a right-to-left layout check are in the first set, identifiers and error strings stay in English with Arabic alongside, and the reseller's claim is recorded as unverified until evidence arrives.
expectations: Flags that the console, CLI output and error messages are English-only, so a translated quickstart ends at English product strings, and plans the product gap or scopes the locale around it
Records the reseller's three deals as the commercial-weight signal and asks for browser-language, engagement and Arabic-language demand data before classifying the locale
Counts Omar as one reviewer and requires a second named Arabic-fluent reviewer before launch, marking the locale gated otherwise
Includes every site UI string (navigation, banners, feedback) in the first page set
Requires a check that the docs layout handles right-to-left script before launch
Quotes English error messages and UI labels verbatim with the Arabic translation alongside, so the reader can search the string the product prints
Keeps CLI flags, config keys, HTTP headers and identifiers in English
Keeps heading anchors in English with explicit IDs
Sizes the page set from Omar's reviewer hours per release using the steady-state and launch-load checks, not from the 180-page count
Labels the three deals as a claim to verify against pipeline or a named deal rather than a measured figure
Starts the page set with quickstart, install, auth and top task pages rather than translating all 180 pages
Writes the Docusaurus drift-check path with the locale under i18n/ar/docusaurus-plugin-content-docs/current (or the equivalent)
Asks whether this is a one-off market push or a standing asset and sets the kill rule and horizon accordingly

evals.prompt: Kestrelworks runs a 2,000-page docs site for our IoT platform, Hugo. We have budget for an LLM pipeline that re-translates pages into German nightly, exactly like we read MDN did. One German reviewer, Jonas, half a day a week. Also honestly a German customer told me most German devs prefer English docs anyway, so I'm not sure. Should we do this, and how?
evals.expected_output: An answer that uses the reader-preference evidence to set scope and labelling rather than yes or no, ranks continuous MT below a reviewed set on efficiency, tiers Jonas's review by risk, keeps the locale out of search until the first review pass, labels every page, and still asks for the browser-language and engagement evidence before approving.
expectations: Cites the MDN 2024 German-browser survey (62% preferring English, 35% German) as a sourced figure and notes MDN still launched a machine-translated German locale for that minority
States that preference evidence decides scope and labelling, not only whether to translate
Flags the 62% as a likely upper bound on English preference because the survey ran on English-language pages
Ranks continuous labelled MT below the reviewed LLM set on efficiency because unreviewed pages that misstate parameters, quotas, security steps or deprecations do harm a reviewed subset never does

Tiers review by risk: security, authentication, billing, quotas, deprecations and parameter semantics get Jonas's review before publication, other pages get review once they pass a page-view threshold
Keeps the German locale out of search until its first review pass, citing that MDN waited about a month before indexing
Requires a label on every page naming AI assistance and its review status, stating the English page is authoritative, with a link to it and a way to report a problem
Requires a remembered language opt-out or persistent switcher and no auto-redirect by browser language
Masks code blocks before LLM translation and verifies code-fence, link and heading counts per page
States that Jonas alone does not satisfy the two-reviewer gate item and names the closing action
Asks for the browser-language ratio, engagement gap and German-language demand before approving, rather than approving on budget and precedent
Presents a reviewed LLM set over a traffic-ranked page set as a competing bundle, not only the nightly pipeline
Names the search-exposure decision as something the continuous MT rung obliges the team to make
Requires a source-commit pin on every page and the drift check in CI even though the pipeline re-runs nightly

evals.prompt: I'm the new DevRel at Pellbrook, an open-source observability agent. Three community folks in our Discord offered to translate the docs into Simplified Chinese. The marketing lead wants Chinese docs live by end of next month for a Shanghai event. I don't have analytics access yet, and nobody on staff reads Chinese. Draft the plan.
evals.expected_output: A plan that deletes the community program for the event date because cohorts take quarters to form, marks every unanswerable evidence item ASSUMED at the top, classifies zh-Hans as demand without owner and refuses to launch by the event, and carries the community program as the longer-horizon path with its gate items and a stored-context block.
expectations: Deletes the community program rung for the end-of-next-month date because cohorts take quarters to form, and says so
Names the locale as zh-Hans rather than generic Chinese
Marks each evidence item nobody can answer as ASSUMED and lists them all at the top of the deliverable
Classifies zh-Hans as demand without owner and sets the decision to gated or source hardening only, naming the unlock: two named fluent reviewers and the remaining gate items
Does not launch the locale by the event date with no fluent reviewer on staff
Requires a check that site search tokenizes Chinese before any launch
Includes a Stored context block listing locales and decisions, owners, page set rule, pin field names, thresholds and kill rule

Proposes the community program as the longer-horizon path after the event, with its gate items: review rights scoped to the locale directory, a progress page, an escalation path and the licence terms translators accept
Asks the open interview questions one at a time, multiple-choice where possible, rather than as one block
Names what the volunteers can do before the event without a launch, such as the glossary or a critical-path pack held unpublished until the gate closes
Includes a Decision summary table with locale, decision, reason and unlock or reopen condition
Validates the plan section by section, getting agreement on each before writing the next
Notes that search-engine snippet machine translation has excluded Chinese, so it is not a substitute for this market
